newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS ANNOUNCE RE-SIGNING OF COACH JACKSON.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS ANNOUNCE RE-SIGNING OF COACH JACKSON.

text.p: The reigning NBA champion Chicago Bulls announced Wednesday that head coach Phil Jackson re-signed with the team for the 1997-98 season.

"Phil told me he wanted to come back for one last year and try to defend our world championship," team chairman Jerry Reinsdorf said in a statement. "It has always been our intention to bring back Phil for that last season and then turn our attention to building for the future."
Reinsdorf said the one-year pact made Jackson the highest-paid "pure" coach in the league, which excluded coaches who also act as their teams' general managers.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed.

Signing Jackson, the Bulls coach in all five of their championships in the past seven years, was considered essential to lure back superstar Michael Jordan who had said he would retire rather than play for another coach.
Jordan made $30.1 million last season and unconfirmed speculation has him asking for anywhere from $36 million to $40 million for the 1997-98 season.
Last season, Jackson became the third coach in league history to win five championships, joining Red Auerbach (nine) and John Kundla (five).

"I'm grateful for a team that loves to work together and with a great coaching staff, we are once again prepared to conquer that monster -- an NBA title," Jackson said from his home in Montana in a statement released through his agent.
"I am pleased that Jerry Reinsdorf and the management of the Bulls have concurred and will allow us a chance to do it once again."
Jackson, 51, has a career record of 96-35 in the postseason and his .733 winning percentage is the best in NBA playoff history.

He guided the team to an NBA-record 72 wins in the 1995-96 regular season and Chicago registered 69 wins this season. The Bulls are 30-8 in the postseason over the last two years, closing out the last two titles with NBA Finals wins over the Seattle SuperSonics and Utah Jazz.
Jackson has a career record of 483-173 in eight seasons as Bulls coach. He was an assistant with Chicago for two seasons prior to being named head coach in 1989.
